paper.title: Paper 4 Programming Practice · Original English Sample
paper.description: [local-paper4-english-v2] Three original programming tasks inspired by common Paper 4 skills. This is not a Cambridge paper or marking scheme.

questions.title: A twenty-place circular queue
questions.statement: Create a fixed array of 20 slots for positive integers. At the start, every slot contains -1 and HeadPointer, TailPointer and NumberItems are -1, -1 and 0. Implement Enqueue(value) and Dequeue() so the pointers wrap around correctly. Enqueue returns False when full or when the value is not positive; Dequeue returns -1 when empty. In the main program, try to add 1 to 25, remove two values and print the accepted and rejected counts and the removed values. Keep your final source and a run record for teacher review.

questions.title: Separate records into six colour files
questions.statement: The supplied TheData.txt has 72 rows. Each row is an integer followed by a comma and one of red, green, blue, orange, yellow or pink. Implement ReadData, SplitData and StoreData. The final program must maintain six files named Red.txt, Green.txt, Blue.txt, Orange.txt, Yellow.txt and Pink.txt. Append matching integers in their original order, one per line, preserving any lines already in those files. Skip malformed rows and print the number of valid records processed. Each test run begins in an independent file workspace, so prior test runs cannot affect one another. Retain your code and file evidence for teacher review.

stages.title: Named routines and file handling
stages.description: Teacher reviews the ReadData, SplitData and StoreData decomposition and file-handling choices.

stages.title: Complete 72-record run
stages.description: All six output files and the processed count are checked against the supplied data.

stages.title: Append, sparse colours and malformed rows
stages.description: Tests check that existing file lines are retained and malformed rows do not stop processing.

stages.title: Code and output evidence
stages.description: Teacher checks that the final source and generated files are retained.

questions.title: Build and traverse a binary search tree
questions.statement: Implement a Node class containing an integer value and left/right child references, and a Tree class with insert and inorder methods. Smaller values go left; equal or larger values go right. The inorder method returns a list produced by recursive traversal. The main program reads space-separated integers and prints the inorder values on one line. Keep your implementation and test evidence for teacher review.

stages.title: Class design and recursive method
stages.description: Teacher reviews the Node/Tree source, recursion and clarity.

stages.title: Insertion and duplicate direction
stages.description: Isolated drivers import the candidate module and inspect tree links.

stages.title: Recursive inorder traversal
stages.description: Isolated drivers call inorder with varied trees; the main program is also run.

stages.title: Code and run evidence
stages.description: Teacher checks the submitted source and retained test run.
